newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE HOPING FOR IRISH RETURN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE HOPING FOR IRISH RETURN.

text.p: World record try-scorer David Campese headed for Ireland on Sunday determined to win another test recall after Australia's modest 29-19 victory over Scotland at Murrayfield.

Campese, who last month earned his 100th international cap against Italy, watched his team mates' efforts from the replacements' bench and has his sights set on a return against Ireland in Dublin on November 23.
"It hasn't done my chances any harm ...now it's up to me," said Campese, who says he will retire for the final time after the Wallabies' current tour of Europe.
The 34-year-old winger has fond memories of Lansdowne Road where he left the All Blacks floundering in his wake during a 1991 World Cup semifinal.
There was no such magic on display on a beautiful autumn afternoon at Murrayfield in an encounter which did nothing to flatter either side.
Australian coach Greg Smith blamed French referee Patrick Thomas for failing to let the game flow but the Scots refused to point the finger at the official.
"We have no-one to blame but ourselves," said disappointed coach Richie Dixon.
Campese's Randwick team mate David Knox, who tried his best to launch his backs in a cluttered midfield, admitted the Wallabies would be seeking a big improvement on the Irish leg of their tour.

"It was a very frustrating game for us...I wouldn't give us more than five out of 10," said the fly-half, who won only his seventh cap in 11 years. "We've got to be scoring eights and we're capable of it."

Yet after a week of lengthy injury bulletins and criticism from some sources at home, even Knox agreed a victory brought a measure of relief. "If we'd have lost, we'd have been sitting in the dressing-room crying," he said.
There will still be pressure on Smith to consider changes for the remaining tests, with plenty of debate likely over flanker and scrum-half and on the wings.

Captain John Eales, at least, had another splendid game, while Matthew Burke underlined his claim to be one of world rugby's outstanding full-backs. His five penalties and two conversions earned him 19 points, boosting his tally in his last two tests to 39.
Warwick Waugh and Daniel Herbert were the Wallaby try-scorers on a day when ACT flanker Owen Finegan gained a less welcome footnote in rugby history.
Finegan became the first uninjured player to be officially substituted in an international when he was hauled off in favour of Brett Robinson with 15 minutes left.
Luckily for several Scots, coach Dixon is not a fan of the International Board's new relaxed rules on replacements. The only home player to leave the field was Gary Armstrong with damaged ribs.
